newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mostly up on rebound.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mostly up on rebound.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up in slow trading on Tuesday due to a technical rebound on short-covering by retail investors, traders said.
The most active September contract was the only one to fall. It ended at 3,325 yuan per tonne, down three yuan. It opened at 3,320 and hit an intraday high of 3,330 and a low of 3,316.
March rose 25 to 3,105, May did not trade, July put on 10 to 3,330, September fell three to 3,325, November increased three to 3,332 and January 1998 was up one to 3,340 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 19,400 tonnes from 19,600.
Traders described the day's rises as a technical rebound after falls in the past few sessions, but said soybean contracts were likely to fall further in the short term.
"Some speculators liquidated their short positions for quick profits today after successive losses over the past few days," one trader said.
"Market sentiment has not improved despite the rebound, and trading was still slow given the absence of market-moving news," he added.
